disease_label_per_paper: Intrathoracic rupture of amebic liver abscess with pleural effusion and portal vein thrombosis
presentation_summary: Bisexual Japanese man with well-controlled HIV infection presented with two weeks of severe right shoulder pain progressing to right upper quadrant abdominal pain.
Admission vital signs were temperature 38.0 degC, blood pressure 120/85 mmHg, heart rate 111/min, respiratory rate 18/min, and oxygen saturation 97% on ambient air.
Exam showed right upper abdominal tenderness and rigidity, decreased breath sounds and dullness at the right lower lung field.
Labs showed WBC 16.02 x 10^9/L with neutrophil predominance, CD4 count 476/uL, INR 1.09, D-dimer 2.6 ug/mL, AST 46 U/L, ALT 64 U/L, LDH 288 U/L, ALP 148 U/L, GGT 99 U/L, and CRP 16.1 mg/dL.

CT chest/abdomen showed a solitary right-lobe liver abscess extending beyond the liver capsule with diaphragmatic disruption, right pleural thickening/fluid, intercostal muscle enlargement, and adjacent portal vein branch thrombosis.
Stool microscopy and antigen testing were negative, but E. histolytica was detected by stool PCR; later qPCR confirmed E. histolytica DNA in stool, liver abscess aspirate, and pleural fluid.

Despite metronidazole, pleural effusion and oxygen demand worsened, requiring pleural and hepatic drainage; the patient improved, received paromomycin and edoxaban after stabilization, and had complete radiologic resolution without recurrence at six months.

quality_warnings: The PubMed/abstract text and body text differ on age; this JSON follows the case-presentation body, which states 40-year-old.
Day-2 respiratory worsening is represented by oxygen_requirement_level because the paper reported 5 L/min nasal cannula but did not report a measured SpO2 at that time.
Neutrophil predominance is retained in presentation_summary and source text but not assigned a synthetic numeric ANC because no percentage was reported.
